answer: The system deploys a rotating beacon at the edge of a canyon, requiring each new agent to prove it can interrogate the beacon’s returning signals across shifting tide patterns. Each fake identity must devote a dedicated quantum channel per agent—doubling resource costs for every Sybil—since the beacon’s entropy disrupts all parallel attempts, while color oscillations in the returning transmissions force a one-to-one calibration loop. It’s not pretty, but it’s the only way to stop them.
